cards.f: Narrative title rule if an opening line is given?
Top level content and structure for narrative?
cards.b: Complex, engaging story, deliberate structure, credible characters, tension built and released, satisfying ending.

cards.f: How much can you handle in 350-450 words?
cards.b: 1-2 main characters, 1 setting, short time span, one central problem or decision.
Wars, invasions or five-suspect murders collapse into summary.
Starting at a dramatic moment, then filling in background briefly.
Present moment, memory, back to the present, changed.
Ending mirrors the opening with new meaning.
Reader knows less than the narrator; reveal at the end, prepared by clues.
Slow pace at key moments, short sentences, sensory focus on small details, delay, foreshadowing.
An early detail that matters later.
'She folded the letter into smaller and smaller squares' rather than 'She was nervous'.
'It was all a dream', meaningless sudden deaths, a final sentence explaining the moral.
Inside the speech marks: "I'm not going," she said.

gaps.s: An early detail that matters later is called ___.
Starting a story at a dramatic moment is 'in ___ res'.
In dialogue, a new speaker begins on a new ___.
A main character needs a want and an ___.
A story should cover a short time ___.
An ending that appears from nowhere, such as 'it was all a ___', should be avoided.
Slow down at key moments and speed up through unimportant time to control ___.

short.q: State three limits to keep a 350-450 word story controlled. [3]
short.model: One or two main characters, one setting, short time span (and one central problem).

short.q: Explain 'show, don't tell' with an example. [2]
short.model: Show feelings through actions, e.g. folding a letter into small squares rather than saying 'she was nervous'.

short.q: State two ways to build tension. [2]
short.model: Short sentences at the crisis, and sensory focus on small details such as a dripping tap.

short.q: Why is 'it was all a dream' a weak ending? [2]
short.model: It is not prepared by clues and feels cheap, so the ending is not earned.
